events.excerpt:
## Overview

llama.cpp v1.1.0 adds the Inkling 2 family (base, Mini and DSpark), Domyn Edge 4B, Zaya1 8B, RAON-1-mini and Hy4 flash, splits DFlash speculative decoding into separate draft methods, and deprecates the old `llama_batch` API in favour of `llama_batch_ext`. It brings a large set of TTS and audio models (Kokoro, Zonos3-Mini, tiny-voca, VoxCPM2, MiniMax-Music3, YuE2, Fish S2, Higgs v3/VibeVoice-ASR and Kyutai Hibiki), token-aware chat parsing, named tool choice, automatic per-tensor quantization targeting a bpw or size budget, a slot-scheduling refactor in `llama-server`, a redesigned Llama Chat web UI with voice messages and agent traces, and updates `ggml` to v1.1.1.

### API changes

- llama.h: deprecate the old `llama_batch` API in favour of `llama_batch_ext` and `llama_process` ([#32306](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/32306), [#32356](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/32356))
- llama.h: add `llama_dflash_variant` and `llama_model_dflash_variant()` for the four DFlash draft heads ([#32016](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/32016))
- llama.h: add `llama_model_meta_arr_n()` and `llama_model_meta_arr_str()` to read GGUF string arrays

arXiv:2611.33162v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Agentic benchmarks report a success rate that confounds distinct causes of failure: misreading the environment, never working out how components of the environment operates, operating the components in the wrong order, and failing to recover from a mistake, each of which calls for a different fix. We present an early preview of MultiNet v2.0-Gridworld - an interactive maze environment built for attribution rather than ranking. Four different types of mechanisms, namely key-door pairs, switch-gate pairs, distractors and decoys, and ordered combinations of these mechanisms, can be added, modified, or removed independently while the renderer, the action space, and the scoring function stay fixed. A breadth-first search over the joint state of position, facing direction, inventory, and mechanism state gives every instance an exact optimal action count, which sets its difficulty and grades unfinished episodes. We fix the evaluation protocol on 15 held-out mazes over 540 episodes, then evaluate three vision-language models on 50 mazes. They solve 6 of 150 episodes, 45 of the 50 mazes were not solved by any model, and no episode containing

events.excerpt:
### Features

* **api:** add Google-managed data controls for Google Cloud projects
* **api:** add Google-managed data controls for user profiles
* **api:** add support for compliance review cases, notices, and items


### Bug Fixes

* **client:** honor proxy and trust_env when proxy variables are set

  `DefaultHttpxClient` and `DefaultAsyncHttpxClient` read `HTTP_PROXY`, `HTTPS_PROXY`, `ALL_PROXY` and `NO_PROXY` even when the caller passed `proxy=` or `trust_env=False`, and the variables won. Now `proxy=` is used for every request and the variables are not read, and `trust_env=False` ignores them, as in plain `httpx2`.

  What you may notice: with `proxy=` set, a host listed in `NO_PROXY` used to be reached directly and now goes through your proxy. To keep a host off the proxy, pass `mounts={"all://that.host": None}`.


### Chores

* **docs:** drop the provisional naming note from the Google Cloud client README
* **docs:** name both causes of the tool use limit error
* **docs:** update example workspace and API key IDs


### Documentation

* show what enum values mean

Because these pitfalls are common, if you’ve worked on any AI product, you’ve probably seen them before.

1. Use generative AI when you don't need generative AI

events.excerpt: We present Depth Pro 2, an approach to estimating dense metric depth for images and video at full resolution. By analyzing prior methods for monocular depth estimation, we find that they commonly trade off temporal consistency and boundary sharpness: multi-frame methods favor consistency, single-frame methods favor sharpness. To overcome this trade-off, we train a single, scalable network that processes both images and video and predicts depth maps at native resolution. Depth Pro 2 produces depth maps that are metrically accurate, sharp, and temporally consistent all at once, outperformingâ¦

Abstract: Audio-video (AV) deepfakes can fake the face, the voice, or both. Most benchmarks only ask whether a clip is real or fake, so they cannot show whether a detector relies on the picture, the voice, or encoding traces. We present MOZAIC, a paired benchmark with a 4-way label in which every source clip is released in all four combinations of real or fake video and real or fake audio so each modality contribution can be measured directly. Fakes cover inner-face swapping, whole-frame video diffusion and voice conversion. MOZAIC has 137,745 clips from 15,014 source pairs and four tasks: T1 AV authenticity, T2 manipulation type, T3 identity verification and T4 explanation. We evaluate 12 AV multimodal LLMs (MLLMs), train four detectors and fine-tune MLLMs with LoRA. Overall, the best MLLM reaches only 35.6% on the four-way T1 and catches far more video-only fakes than voice-only fakes (43.6% vs 7.5%). sqlite3_rsync: Database Remote-Copy Tool For SQLite

This additional SQLite tool has been around for a while now - it was added as "experimental" in SQLite 3.47.0 in October 2024 and enhanced in SQLite 3.50.0 in May 2025. It was only today that I understood one of its most attractive characteristics.

Normally, if you want to grab a snapshot copy of a SQLite database, you need to use either the backup API or VACUUM INTO. In both cases you need enough disk space to create a duplicate copy of your database, so if you're on a small instance and you already use more than half of the available disk you are plain out of luck.

sqlite3_rsync can copy a snapshot of your database over an SSH connection to another machine, without first needing to create a full local copy!

It's also good for synchronizing an existing copy of a database without re-transmitting t

# Patch release v5.24.1

A patch to fix a bunch of stuff for vLLM, a few distributed issues, and some model fixes (llama4, dory); see the full list

### vLLM related
- Fix backward compatibility of the cache rename for remote code (#51085) by @hmellor
- Restore modeling_attn_mask_utils for remote code (one-off to unblock vLLM) (#51124) by @hmellor 
- Expose past_key_values in MBartDecoderLayer.forward signature for remote code (#51177) by @hmellor 
- [OmniASR] Support a padding_mask kept on the CPU in the audio encoder (#51100) by @El-euchidali

### Model fixes
- Fix Llama4 forward crash on missing image_outputs (#51144) by @kylesayrs
- Fix dory static cache (#50993) by @ArthurZucker 

### Distributed
- Allow expert parallelism alone with tp_plan={} (#50996) by @3outeille 
- Fix strided checkpoint reads on PyTorch 2.9 (#51042) by @satsuki2486441738

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/compare/v5.24.0...v5.24.1
